worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & -4 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a}=-1\pm 2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's consider the eigenvalue $\lambda =-1+2\text{i}.$ We can immediately construct the rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 
$(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.$ 
In our case, we have $\,{\lambda }_{1}=-1+2\text{i},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1+2\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & -1+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2-2\text{i} & -4 \\ 2 & 2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}(-2-2\text{i}){x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+(2-2\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the matrix $A-\lambda I$ is singular, the system above has a non-trivial solution. This implies that one row is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables as free. For example, from the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}=-(1-\text{i}){x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}-(1-\text{i}){x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=-1$, we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we can construct the matrix $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\frac{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}{{c}^{2}+{d}^{2}}=\frac{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}=2.
$$
